Black Friday is upon us and it's a great time to grab yourself a new monitor. Whether you're looking for a new OLED monitor for gaming, editing, or anything else, this deals weekend is the perfect opportunity to upgrade your setup and your display.

We're looking at all the major retailers and bringing you live, up-to-the-minute recommendations from likes of Amazon, Newegg, Best Buy, and beyond, using our testing data and years of hands-on reviewing experience to make recommendations. If you want even more options, we also have our list of Best Gaming Monitors and our Black Friday Gaming Monitor Deals hub, but we're putting the hottest deals in this blog.

With AI driving up the price of SSDs, RAM, and GPUs, buying a monitor is a much better way to upgrade your setup. Adding an OLED to your gaming rig will drastically improve how your games look without breaking the bank. Here are all the best deals!

Quick Links: Black Friday Monitor Deals

Amazon: Up to $500 off Gaming Monitors

Dell: The best monitor deals from Dell - up to $100 off

Hottest Black Friday OLED Monitor Deals

MO27Q28G 27-Inch WOLED Gaming Monitor: was $599.99 now $399.99
Gigabyte's 27-inch MO27Q28G gaming monitor features a fast 280Hz refresh rate and a 0.03ms response time on its colorful 4th-Gen WOLED display with 99.5% of the DCI-P3 color gamut. High pixel density delivers a crisp image at QHD resolution. View Deal

ROG XG27AQDMGR 27-inch WOLED Gaming Monitor: was $599 now $529
Asus' ROG XG27AQDMGR 27-inch gaming monitor is a flat-panel WOLED display with a crisp 1440p (QHD) resolution and a super-fast 240Hz refresh rate. Enjoy smooth-motion gameplay with a 0.03ms response time and a glossy screen finish. View Deal

The Acer Predator X27U W1 is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium and includes two HDMI 2.1 and two DisplayPort 1.4 ports. View Deal

The Innocn 2780S is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It covers 99% of sRGB and DCI-P3 and offers peak brightness of 400 nits. View Deal

The Gigabyte GO27Q24G is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and an MLA+ WOLED panel. It features a RealBlack Glossy display, a 4-sided borderless design, and can hit 1,300 nits peak brightness. View Deal

The AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2 is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync and offers a peak brightness of 1,000 nits. View Deal

Hottest Black Friday Other Monitor Types Deals

34" Odyssey G5 (G55H): was $379.99 now $249.99
The Samsung Odyssey G5 (G55H) is a 34-inch WQHD gaming monitor with a 1000R curve and a VA panel. The monitor maxes out at 180 Hz and supports AMD FreeSync Premium. View Deal

27” Odyssey G5 (G53F): was $249.99 now $169.99
The Samsung Odyssey G5 (G53F) is a 27-inch gaming monitor featuring a QHD IPS panel and a 200 Hz refresh rate. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium with a maximum brightness rating of 300 nits. View Deal

34" ViewFinity S50GC Series Ultra-WQHD: was $329.99 now $199.99
One of the most popular deals on Amazon right now, get this 34-inch ViewFinity monitor from Samsung for just $219, a return to its lowest-ever price. Comes with a 100Hz refresh rate, WQHD resolution, HDR10 support, AMD FreeSync, and more. View Deal

TUF Gaming 27-Inch Gaming Monitor (VG27AQ): was $209 now $168.99
This gaming monitor from Asus spans 27 inches across and features an IPS panel. It has a dense, QHD resolution and a 180 Hz refresh rate, which are great specs for gaming. It also has both DisplayPort and HDMI input options. View Deal

27-inch Odyssey G30D 180Hz Gaming Monitor: was $229.99 now $119.99
This 27-inch Samsung gaming screen isn't much more expensive than an office monitor. But it sports a 180 Hz refresh rate, 1ms response time, and FreeSync variable refresh. It's a VA panel, which generally means better contrast and deeper blacks than TN or IPS, but viewing angles likely aren't the best. View Deal

The MSI MAG 272URDFA E16 is a 27-inch gaming monitor that packs in a dense 4K (3840 x 2160) resolution. The monitor tops out at a 320 Hz refresh rate (when operating at FHD resolution); otherwise, it's 160 Hz at its native 4K resolution. View Deal

The Acer Nitro VG270K is a 27-inch dual-mode 4K gaming monitor. It operates at a 160 Hz refresh rate at its native 4K resolution, but dropping down to FHD resolution boosts that figure to 320 Hz. View Deal

November 27, 2026 – 6:46 AM Black Friday has begun and we're tracking all the very best deals on OLED gaming monitors, productivity monitors, and more!

November 27, 2026 – 6:47 AM Buying a monitor over Black Friday could be one of the best ways to elevate your gaming setup. In 2026, PC component pricing means that upgrades to RAM, SSDs, and GPUs are much more expensive than they used to be. Monitors, by contrast, are cheaper. So, you could spend less and upgrade your viewing experience in a number of different ways. You could get a larger monitor for more immersive viewing and multitasking, upgrade to a higher refresh rate for more frame headroom, or increase your resolution for more detail. Of course, you could also make the leap to OLED, one of the biggest upgrades you can make to gaming right now.

November 27, 2026 – 7:08 AM 500Hz, 27-inch QD-OLED Innocn gaming monitor drops to $475

If you're looking for a panel that doesn't compromise on pure refresh rates, Innocn's GA27M1Q QD-OLED display might be just the panel you're after. Sporting a 27-inch size, QHD resolution, and a blisteringly fast 500Hz refresh rate, this display's got heaps of gaming performance under the hood, especially if you play esports-focused titles like Valorant or Counter-Strike 2.

27-inch QD-OLED GA27M1Q 500Hz gaming monitor: was $599 now $474.98
Offering a 2560 x 1440p resolution, in addition to dual HDMI 2.1 ports and DisplayPort 1.4, as well as 1x USB-B upstream and 2x Type-A downstream ports, this panel offers performance without the premium price, thanks to its rapid 500Hz refresh rate and support for FreeSync and G-Sync. View Deal

Expect a sweet spot between performance and resolution here. With the display's 256 x 1440p resolution and refresh rate, you'll want a fairly powerful system with a decent CPU under the hood to reliably saturate the monitor here. One important note is that the semi-gloss display isn't actually all that bright when compared to more expensive competitors. While you do get a 0.03ms GtG response time, the GA27M1Q's SDR brightness tops out at 300 nits. However, considering the wealth of other features on offer here, it might be a fine trade for a very well rounded panel that's almost garaunteed to look fantastic with deep blacks and a near-infinite contrast ratio. — Sayem Ahmed

November 27, 2026 – 7:20 AM Grab 36% off this 32-inch, 4K, 240Hz Samsung Odyssey G8 display at Woot

If our last Samsung Odyssey deal didn't grab your attention, this one certainly will. The Samsung Odyssey OLED G8 monitor is 36% off at Woot, pushing the price down to $699.99. New customers get that extra $60 discount, meaning you can save heaps on a flagship-level 4K display without breaking the bank entirely.

Odyssey OLED G8 32-inch 240Hz OLED gaming monitor: was $1099 now $699
Extra $60 off for new Woot customers

The Samsung Odyssey OLED G8 offers a 3840 x 2160 resolution, 240Hz refresh rate, 1x HDMI 2.1 port, 1x DisplayPort 1.4, 1x USB-C (DP Alt Mode with 98W PD), 2x USB-A 3.2 downstream ports, and a 3.5mm headphone jack. View Deal

Getting a 4K OLED display with as many features as this, and at this price point, doesn't come around too often. Sporting up to 1000 nits of peak brightness, this 4K display has almost everything you could want out of an OLED monitor. The only thing missing in its feature set is built-in speakers, but that's nothing a set of cheap freestanding desktop speakers can't fix.

Expect Samsung OLED Safeguard+ to prevent burn-in, in addition to a height-adjustable swivel stand, VESA mount, and all of the gaming features you want, like VRR support, as well as FreeSync Premium Pro and G-Sync compatibility. This should be your next main monitor upgrade, if you've got the cash to spare. — Sayem Ahmed
